newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK CANCELS INNOVATION BANK'S LICENSE.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK CANCELS INNOVATION BANK'S LICENSE.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that it had driven the final nail into the coffin of Innovation Bank, revoking its license and closing one of the final chapters of the country's banking crisis.
"The board of the Bank of Lithuania decided to cancel the banking license of Innovation Bank from May 26, 1997," the central bank said in a statement.
The central bank also said that Innovation's losses amounted to a staggering 403.177 million litas as of April 1 1997.
It added that the bank's capital was minus 378.096 million litas as of April 1 1997.
The central bank said that the bank was not meeting its risk limit requirements.
Innovation's shock closure in late 1995 sparked a crisis in the country's banking sector and brought down a prime minister.
The bank tried to rise from the grave last year but was kept under by a crippling bad loan portfolio.
The Lithuanian parliament decided in April to close the bank for good and the government said it would assume the obligations to its depositors.
